preview.overview: BYU brings the lineal championship belt to Lawrence as the current holder, looking to extend their reign against a Kansas team hungry to reclaim it. The Jayhawks have owned this matchup historically, winning three straight meetings including a 17-13 victory in 2024, but BYU arrives as the belt-holder with momentum from a 28-24 win over Notre Dame.
key_matchups: BYU's inconsistency on the road versus Kansas's home field advantage and recent upset potential
Kansas's defensive performance against BYU's balanced attack, given the Jayhawks held them to just 13 points last November
Turnover margin in a matchup where both teams have shown vulnerability to close losses
preview.betting_angles: Kansas's recent form is decidedly mixed—they've lost three of their last five, though they did upset Baylor 25-24 at home and demolished West Virginia 37-14. BYU has been equally inconsistent on the road, losing at Utah 20-28 and at UCF 31-39, but they've now won two straight including a signature victory over Notre Dame. The series history strongly favors Kansas, who won all three previous matchups and most recently held BYU to 13 points in 2024, suggesting defensive execution could prove decisive.
preview.prediction_writeup: Kansas's historical dominance in this series is too significant to ignore, especially with the Jayhawks playing at home where they've shown they can execute defensively—their 13-point effort against BYU last year proves they know how to contain this offense. BYU's road struggles are a real concern; losses at Utah and UCF this season suggest they don't travel well, and Kansas's ability to win tight games at home (25-24 over Baylor) gives them an edge in a close contest. While BYU's recent win over Notre Dame is impressive, the weight of Kansas's three-game series advantage, the home field, and BYU's documented road fragility point to a Jayhawks upset that would return the belt to Lawrence.
